observations: The page number «15» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. L01-L06 end chapter 18 (p. 14, JP2 0046): the apogee of Mars four signs, 8 degrees, 24 minutes; of Venus two signs, 21 degrees, 15 minutes; of Mercury seven signs, 14 degrees, 54 minutes; the apogee of the moon moves, by 6′ 40″ 18‴ 48⁗ a day and 16″ 42‴ 27⁗ an hour. L07, L16 and L21: the headings of chapters 19-21, in bold, centred.

In the apparatus the readings of C and M are given as figures with the units printed small above them: S or s (signa), G or g (gradus), P or p (minutes, partes), M or m (seconds, minuta), «delidhe», «thelidhe», «thelidae», «thelithae», «thel.» (thirds, the Arabic thālitha), Q (quartae), «rabe» (fourths, rābiʿa), and once «secundae», «tertiae», «quartae» (N12). They are transcribed {st:LABEL|VALUE}, the label above the value; the readings of C in N03 have the capital labels S G P M, those of M the small ones.

Checked: the hourly motions against the daily ones divided by twenty-four. The sun: 59′ 8″ a day (L22-L23) gives 2′ 27″ 50‴ an hour; the text's 2′ 27″ 50‴ 25⁗ (L23-L24) is the twenty-fourth part of 59′ 8″ 10‴, a daily motion with 10 thirds, which the text does not state. The node of the moon: 3′ 11″ 48‴ a day (L13-L14) gives 7″ 59‴ 30⁗ an hour; the text's 7″ 57‴ (L15) is the twenty-fourth part of 3′ 10″ 48‴. The apogee of the moon: 6′ 40″ 18‴ 48⁗ a day (L04) gives 16″ 40‴ 47⁗; the text's 16″ 42‴ 27⁗ (L06) is the twenty-fourth part of 6′ 40″ 58‴ 48⁗. The moon: 13° 10′ 34″ 52‴ 48⁗ a day (L17-L18) gives 32′ 56″ 27‴ 12⁗; the text's 32′ 56″ 47‴ 52⁗ (L19-L20) is the twenty-fourth part of 13° 10′ 43″ 8‴ 48⁗. The readings of C and M in notes 6, 7, 19, 20, 22, 23, 25 and 26 give the same figures as the text.

L02: «eltheniae 0», the figure zero; the lemma of note 2 ends with the letter o, «Veneris . . . . o]», at the height of the small letters. L11: «eliauzehar» (al-jawzahar, the node) in italics. L13: «(sic)», upright, the editor's. L18: the r of «quartae» is printed without its arm, so that it looks like a dotless ı; transcribed «quartae».

N07: «{i:om.} M;», the semicolon set close to the siglum (3 px); the colons and semicolons of the text stand after the thin space of the edition (11-13 px measured), as does the colon after «marg.» in N09 (11 px). N08: «signorum . . . XLVIII», three points; the other lemmas have four. N09: the first 0 of the reading of note 20, under s, is lighter and thinner than the others.
